content.title: Mark Jones Leaves ESPN for Sacramento Kings - Today in Sacramento
content.text: Got story updates? Submit your updates here. ›A cubist interpretation of a veteran sportscaster's transition to a new role, capturing the energy and dynamism of the moment.Today in SacramentoMark Jones, a 36-year veteran sportscaster at ESPN, is making a surprising move by leaving the network to join the Sacramento Kings as their primary play-by-play announcer. Instead of retiring, Jones has decided to stay in Sacramento, where he has found a new home and family within the Kings organization and the local community. Why it matters Jones' decision to leave ESPN and join the Kings is a testament to the power of community and the warmth of a new home. Sacramento has become a second home for Jones, and his choice to stay and continue his work with the team highlights the importance of finding fulfillment and purpose beyond just the job itself. The details Jones, 64, has been a staple in the sports broadcasting world, known for his extensive vocabulary and distinctive style. He started his career in Canada before joining ESPN to host 'NBA Today'. Over the years, he has become a household name, calling play-by-play for NBA, WNBA, and college football games across the country. However, Jones' decision to stay in Sacramento is not just about the job - it's about the community and the people he has come to know and love. He has found a new family in the Kings organization and the city of Sacramento, and he is eager to continue his work with the team. Jones' final game for ESPN will be on Sunday, April 13, 2026, when the Orlando Magic visits the Boston Celtics.The Kings hired Jones to replace Grant Napear as their primary play-by-play announcer in November 2020.
